title: Operational identity enters the contract through a witness
excerpts: Witnesses are the connection between private off-chain data and your Compact contract.
Witnesses are declared similarly to circuits, but with the witness keyword.

codeBlocks.title: Witness declarations
Syntax detail
codeBlocks.code:
// witness does use parentheses
witness dataName(): Bytes<32>;

title: What gets published and what stays out of chain state
excerpts: A key part of a Compact smart contract is the ledger section, which describes the state kept on-chain.
The example stores a key, a value, the contract state, and a round counter used to preserve anonymity.

codeBlocks.title: Public ledger fields
Syntax detail
codeBlocks.code:
// ledger does not use parentheses
export ledger name: Bytes<32>;

title: The witness keeps the secret and exposes only what is needed
excerpts: In the example contract, the witness secretKey is used to provide the user's private key.
Witness values can contain private information and require disclose() before they can be used in ledger operations.

codeBlocks.title: Using secretKey() inside a circuit

title: Why the witness stays on the local machine
excerpts: The third context is the user's local machine. Compact can call the local context through witnesses.
The witness is not implemented in Compact source code. Instead, its implementation is the responsibility of the DApp TypeScript code.
